entrypoint_hazard.description: Running Python processes retain the pre-successor producer or consumer code. A legacy verifier can continue replacing the shared JSON without the V2 guard, and a legacy executor does not require the V2 guard.

forbidden_actions: do not restart only one of multiple legacy verifier instances and assume the other reloaded
do not start the successor executor while any legacy verifier can still publish
do not reactivate a legacy executor as rollback
do not issue a canary authorization during migration
do not place a routeability or discretionary test order
ordered_activation_steps: open a maintenance window that prevents automatic restart of the verifier and Practice-007 executor
verify the practice account is flat with no pending orders and canary entry_authorized is false with zero authorized entries
stop every legacy Practice-007 executor entrypoint before changing verifier ownership
stop every legacy independent-evidence-verifier entrypoint and verify the process inventory contains zero remaining instances
verify all successor artifact hashes against independent_evidence_verifier_safety_v2_candidate_manifest.json
start exactly one successor verifier and no executor
wait for one V2 guard row whose phase is completed and whose exact pass, owner, generation, timestamp, status, authorization flag, and persisted-byte SHA agree with the JSON
if the completed status is mismatch, leave execution stopped and investigate; never bypass the guard
start exactly one successor Practice-007 executor only after a coherent completed match exists
verify read-only that missing, in-progress, failed, stale, and hash-mismatched guard fixtures are denied without submitting an order
restore supervision only after process inventory confirms one successor verifier and one successor executor
preconditions: candidate manifest hashes match exact workspace bytes
practice account is flat and has no pending orders
canary authorization is disabled and empty
a supervisor maintenance gate prevents legacy auto-restart
operator has an explicit rollback window
rollback: leave canary authorization disabled and empty
preserve JSON, guard, report, and logs for incident review
keep the execution entrypoint stopped until a new reviewed successor is available
